member.name: P:SysWeaver.ApiKeyParams.CredFile
member.summary: Filename, if specified the API key is read from the file (should be single line of text, lines starting with '#' is considered a comment and not read). Takes precedence over . Relative paths are relative to the executable folder. Variables can be used, they start with "$(" and end with ")", see . Variables can be any value of the Environment.SpecialFolder enum, or CLI environment variables plus others. Ex: "$(KeyFolder)/SecretService.txt" Some common folder variables: $(CommonApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by all users. $(LocalApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by the current, non-roaming user. $(ApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data for the current roaming user (typically settings that should be shared between systems). $(MyPictures) = The My Pictures folder. Env info variables: $(Executable) = Full path to the executable, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService.exe" $(ExeAppName) = Name of the executable, ex: "MyService" (this can be different from AppName) $(ExecutableDir) = ExecutableDir, ex: "C:\MyServices" $(ExecutableBase) = Full path to the executable, excluding it's extensions, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService" $(AppName) = Application name (defaults to exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "MyService". $(AppGuid) = A guid derived from the application assembly name (stable between runs) $(AppDisplayName) = Friendly application name (defaults to de-camel cased exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "My service". $(MachineName) = Machine name, ex: "DESKTOP-324VHA". $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored. ex: "C:\Keys".

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ApiKeyParams.GetApiKey(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Get the api key (may be from the supplied file, no caching is done so don't call frequently)
member.param: If true, throw if the key file doesn't exist or if the inline key is empty
member.returns: The API key (trimmed), or null / empty if no key is available and is false
member.exception: is true and the key file doesn't exist, the key file contains no non-comment line, or no file is specified and the inline key is empty.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.ArrayEqualityComparer
member.summary: Creates equality comparers for arrays, two arrays are equal if they have the same length and all elements are equal (using an element comparer).
member.remarks: Two null arrays are equal, a null array is never equal to a non-null array (not even an empty one). Null elements are only equal to other null elements, the element comparer is never called with a null element. The hash code of a null array is 0, null elements doesn't contribute to the hash code (but the element position does).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.ArrayPoolStream
member.summary: A seekable, readable and writable in-memory stream (like MemoryStream) that uses buffers rented from the shared ArrayPool. Dispose the stream when done to return the buffer to the pool. The data can be retrieved without a copy using GetMemory (pooled, dispose the result), GetBuffer, GetBufferMemory or ToArray (the buffer is handed out and never returned to the pool).
member.remarks: Differences from MemoryStream: Position and Seek are clamped to [0, Length] (no exception, and no gap can be created). Buffers that have been handed out are never modified (copy on write). The stream is not thread safe.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.AsciiCase.FindChangeOrNonAscii(System.String,System.UInt16)
member.summary: Check if a string may need a case change. The first chars are checked inline (no call overhead, most mixed case text has a letter to change early), only 128 bit vectors are used, allocating the converted string right after code using 256 bit vectors was measurably slower.
member.param: The string to search
The first letter that must change, or
member.returns: -1 if all chars are ASCII and none must change, else the index of a char that must be inspected: an ASCII letter that must change or a non ASCII char. For the first 32 chars (and strings shorter than 8 chars) it's the first such char. Beyond the first 32 chars an ASCII letter that must change is preferred, the first non ASCII char is only returned if no ASCII letter must change (so a non ASCII char may exist before the returned index). Callers must treat a non ASCII char at the returned index as "check the rest of the string".

member.name: T:SysWeaver.AsyncLock
member.summary: An async lock (a semaphore) that can be held by up to holders at the same time. The lock can be taken async (Lock), synchronously (LockSync) or without waiting (TryLock). All the slots can be taken at once (LockAll, LockAllSync, TryLockAll), giving exclusive access.
member.remarks: The lock is not re-entrant, taking the lock again while holding it (with a max concurrency of one) will dead lock. The returned IDisposable releases the lock, it must be disposed exactly once (the same instance is returned to all holders, so disposing it twice will release a slot owned by someone else).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.BlockUntilChange
member.summary: Provides a mechanism to async wait for a "change". Changes are tracked using a "change id" (a counter) that is incremented by every call.
member.remarks: Typical usage (long polling): a consumer starts with change id 0 and loops calling with the last returned id, a producer calls whenever new data is available. Thread safe, any number of producers and waiters can use the same instance.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.BlockUntilChange.Change
member.summary: Triggers a change, any task waiting for a change on this instance will continue and return a new change id.
member.returns: The new change id (the previous id plus one)
member.remarks: Calling this after still increments the change id, but no waiter is woken (waits return immediately after dispose).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.BlockUntilValueChange

member.name: T:SysWeaver.CachedValue`1
member.summary: Caches a single value with an expiration time, the value is (re-)created by a supplied function when it's missing or expired.
member.typeparam: The type of the cached value
member.remarks: Thread safe. Reading a valid value is lock free, creating a value is serialized by an (so the value is only created once even with concurrent callers). If auto dispose is enabled the previous value is disposed when it's replaced, cleared or pruned (unless the same instance is cached again), exceptions thrown by dispose are recorded in . Values are not reference counted, another thread may have obtained a value just before it's replaced (and may still be using it), so the disposal of a replaced, cleared or pruned value is deferred by (a grace period, by default the cache duration clamped to [10 seconds, 5 minutes]). A value that is used for longer than the grace period after it's replaced can still be disposed while in use, don't use auto dispose for such values. disposes the current value and all values waiting for a deferred disposal immediately. Exceptions thrown by the get function are propagated and nothing is cached. The async methods have overloads with a waitUntilReady argument: when false, a caller that finds the value missing or expired starts an update in the background (unless one is already running) and gets default until the value is ready, instead of waiting.

member.summary: A forward only, read only stream that is the concatenation of several streams (chunks), the chunks are opened lazily (one at a time) and disposed when fully read.
member.remarks: A chunk is considered fully read when a read from it returns 0 bytes, so any kind of chunk stream (including network, pipe and decompression streams that may return short reads) can be used. Seeking, writing and are not supported (throws ), does nothing. The stream is not thread safe. Used by CompressedChunkedStream (SysWeaver.Storage) to read content defined chunks as one stream.

All chars are compared ordinally.

Strings are stored in blocks of strings, each string (except the first in a block) is front coded, i.e. stored as the length of the common prefix with the previous string (max 31) followed by the remaining chars, one byte per char. A binary search on the first string of each block is followed by a linear scan of the block.
Strings must be non-empty and only contain chars in the range [32, 255]; this (and the sort order) is only validated in DEBUG builds, in release builds violating it gives undefined results (chars above 255 are truncated to a byte).
Not thread safe. The read methods (, and enumeration) build the last partial block if needed, so call after the last before reading concurrently from multiple threads.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.CompactAsciiString
member.summary: Class that takes some data and represents it as a compact string. An integer is written in base N (where N is the number of valid chars), least significant digit first, using the ASCII chars [33, 127] (printable chars and DEL) that aren't invalid.
member.remarks: Immutable and thread safe. Typically used through or . The encoding of a value is not padded, so the length of the string depends on the value (0 is a single char). The decoding is not canonical: many strings decode to the same value (trailing zero digits are ignored and too long strings wrap around), so compare the strings or the decoded values, but don't assume that Encode(Decode(s)) == s for strings that weren't made by Encode.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.CompactStringTree
member.summary: A string tree stores a bunch of strings in a way that makes it fast to check if a test string starts with ANY of the contained strings. A memory efficient version of that doesn't store the strings (only a leaf flag per node), found strings are extracted from the text.
member.remarks: The root node is the tree, the leaf flag of the root is used as the case in-sensitive marker. Case in-sensitive trees upper case all chars (invariant culture), and the found strings have the casing of the text (not the added string). Empty strings are not supported, they can't be added (throws an ). Not thread safe for writes (see ). In debug builds every node have a finalizer (used to maintain the AllocatedNodes diagnostics counter, that only exists in debug builds). Not used by the framework.

member.remarks: A typical usage is to limit the number of concurrent tasks when processing a list of items in parallel. member.param: The function to limit, it is replaced with a function that waits for a free slot before calling the original function (it is left unchanged if no limiting is needed)

The maximum number of concurrent operations. If less than zero, it's a percentage of the number of available logical processors (rounded to the nearest integer, at least one). If zero the concurrency is (the number of processors minus one, but at least two). Ex: -50 = 50% of the number of processors (so 4 if there are 8 processors). -200 = 200% of the number of processors (so 16 if there are 8 processors). 0 = Number of processors minus one (so 7 if there are 8 processors).
The number of items that will be processed, the function is only wrapped if it's greater than the computed concurrency (and greater than one)
member.typeparam: The type of the first argument of the function (typically the item)
The type of the second argument of the function
The type of the result of the function

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Config
member.summary: Get process wide configuration settings (key / value pairs) from JSON files, read once when the class is first used. Files are read in this order, later files override keys from earlier files: 1. "[CommonApplicationData]/SysWeaver/DefaultSystemConfig.json", system wide defaults (created with a commented template if missing). 2. "[ExecutableBase].Config.json", the application config (ex: "C:\MyApp\MyApp.Config.json"). 3. "[CommonApplicationData]/SysWeaver/ForcedSystemConfig.json", system wide forced values (created with a commented template if missing).
member.remarks: Only the top level properties of the root JSON object are used. Comments and trailing commas are allowed. Keys are case insensitive. Supported values are strings, numbers, booleans, null and arrays of those. Parse errors are written to the console and otherwise ignored (the file or key is skipped). The system wide files (in "[CommonApplicationData]/SysWeaver", see ) are readable by everyone but only writable by admins / root: missing templates are only created by privileged processes (, other processes just use the defaults), and privileged processes restrict existing files (Windows: owner Administrators, no inherited rules, read for Everyone; Linux: mode 0644) and remove Everyone rules that older versions added to the folder (Windows). Typical keys read through this class are folder settings (see ), ex: "AllFolders", "UserFolders", "KeyFolder", "FileHashFolders".

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Config.SystemConfigFolder
member.summary: The folder of the system wide config files, "[CommonApplicationData]/SysWeaver"

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Config.RestrictToAdmins(System.String)
member.summary: Make a system wide config file readable by everyone but only writable by admins / root. Windows: owned by Administrators, no inherited rules, full control for SYSTEM and Administrators, read for Everyone. Linux: mode 0644 (files written by root are owned by root). Only changes the file if needed, failures are ignored (the process isn't allowed to change it).
member.param: The config file

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Config.IsRestricted(System.Security.AccessControl.FileSecurity,System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier,System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier)
member.summary: True if the file is owned by admins / SYSTEM, doesn't inherit rules and only admins / SYSTEM may change it

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Config.RemoveEveryoneFromSystemConfigFolder
member.summary: Older versions gave Everyone full control of the system config folder ("C:\ProgramData\SysWeaver") itself, so anyone could delete (and recreate) the system wide config files, remove those rules (Windows only). The data folders in it (ex: "Shared") get their own rules (see ).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Config.ApplyConfig(System.Type,System.Object,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Read a JSON config file and assign its values to the matching public instance properties / fields of an object.
member.param: The type whose members are set (normally the type of ).
The instance to update.

The config file name, relative names are relative to "[CommonApplicationData]/SysWeaver". If the file doesn't exist and is not null, a file containing an empty object, the comment and a list of the settable members (with defaults and XML doc summaries if SysWeaver.Docs is available) is created.
Optional comment to write at the top of a generated file, if null no file is generated.
member.remarks: Member names are matched case sensitively. Read only properties, init only fields and members marked with are skipped. Only primitive numeric types, , , and single dimension arrays of those are supported, other members are silently ignored. Values that can't be converted to the member type are ignored. Strings are converted to numbers using the invariant culture ('.' as the decimal separator, no thousands separators, ex: "1.5", "-3", "1e5").

Optional comment to write at the top of a generated file, if null no file is generated.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.CredentialParams.CredFile
member.summary: Filename, if specified the user and password is read from the file (should be single line of text in the user:key format). The first line that doesn't start with '#' is used, the user name is everything before the first ':' and the password everything after it (surrounding white space is trimmed). Takes precedence over and . Relative paths are relative to the executable folder. Variables can be used, they start with "$(" and end with ")", see . Variables can be any value of the Environment.SpecialFolder enum, or CLI environment variables plus others. Ex: "$(KeyFolder)/SecretService.txt" Some common folder variables: $(CommonApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by all users. $(LocalApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by the current, non-roaming user. $(ApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data for the current roaming user (typically settings that should be shared between systems). $(MyPictures) = The My Pictures folder. Env info variables: $(Executable) = Full path to the executable, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService.exe" $(ExeAppName) = Name of the executable, ex: "MyService" (this can be different from AppName) $(ExecutableDir) = ExecutableDir, ex: "C:\MyServices" $(ExecutableBase) = Full path to the executable, excluding it's extensions, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService" $(AppName) = Application name (defaults to exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "MyService". $(AppGuid) = A guid derived from the application assembly name (stable between runs) $(AppDisplayName) = Friendly application name (defaults to de-camel cased exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "My service". $(MachineName) = Machine name, ex: "DESKTOP-324VHA". $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored. ex: "C:\Keys".

member.summary: Get the credentials (may be from the supplied file, no caching is done so don't call frequently)
member.param: The username
The password

If true, throw if the credentials file doesn't exist, contains no non-comment line, or if the user or password is empty. If false, a missing credentials file or a file without any non-comment line yields empty values (and false) without throwing.
member.returns: False if the user or password is empty, else True
member.exception: The first non-comment line of the credentials file has no ':' (regardless of ), or is true and the credentials file doesn't exist, contains no non-comment line, or the user or password is empty.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.DataTypePolicy
member.summary:
Decides which types (serialized) data may name, ex: using "$type" in json, see . Any type that can resolve (in a loaded assembly, an assembly in the executable folder or a trusted platform assembly of the runtime) is allowed, except:
Denied types (see and ), also as an array element or generic argument (ex: List<Process>).
Delegates and reflection types ( including , , , ), unless explicitly allowed using .
A denied type is never allowed (not even if explicitly allowed). and are kept for compatibility, all assemblies are allowed.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Data.CommonTableData.RowCount
member.summary: Rows in the data, this is the first row + number of returned rows + look ahead rows (that are avasilable). Example (page with 20 items, stepping max 3 pages forward at a time): Request: Row = 20 MaxRowCount = 20 LookAhead = 20 * 3 + 1 Response: RowCount = 35 => There are 35 rows total, 15 rows will be returned for page 2 and no more pages exist. RowCount = 50 => There are 50 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3 exists. RowCount = 90 => There are 90 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 100 => There are 100 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 101 => There are at least 101 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5, 6 exists and maybe more pages.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Data.TableDataSearchAttribute
member.summary: Put on a string member to control if (and with what weight) it's used when performing a text search on the rows of a data table. By default the public string fields and properties that are columns (no , hidden columns included) are searched with a weight of 1.
member.remarks: A string member with this attribute (and a positive weight) is searched even if it's non-public or has a , so it can be used to search texts that aren't sent to the client. Members with a weight of zero or less are excluded from the search, the remaining are ordered by descending weight and the rank of a match in a member is multiplied by its weight times 0.95 per preceding searched member (so a weight of 2 counts about twice as much as a weight of 1). Compiler generated members (ex: auto property backing fields) are never searched (put the attribute on the property). Has no effect on members that aren't of type and on members of expanded members.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Data.TableDataOrderRequest.Row
member.summary: The first row to return (zero based index). Example (page with 20 items, stepping max 3 pages forward at a time): Request: Row = 20 MaxRowCount = 20 LookAhead = 20 * 3 + 1 Response: RowCount = 35 => There are 35 rows total, 15 rows will be returned for page 2 and no more pages exist. RowCount = 50 => There are 50 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3 exists. RowCount = 90 => There are 90 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 100 => There are 100 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 101 => There are at least 101 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5, 6 exists and maybe more pages.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Data.TableDataOrderRequest.MaxRowCount
member.summary: The maximum number of rows to return. 0 = All rows. Example (page with 20 items, stepping max 3 pages forward at a time): Request: Row = 20 MaxRowCount = 20 LookAhead = 20 * 3 + 1 Response: RowCount = 35 => There are 35 rows total, 15 rows will be returned for page 2 and no more pages exist. RowCount = 50 => There are 50 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3 exists. RowCount = 90 => There are 90 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 100 => There are 100 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5 exists. RowCount = 101 => There are at least 101 rows total, 20 rows will be returned for page 2 and a page 3, 4, 5, 6 exists and maybe more pages.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.EnvInfo.TextVars
member.summary: Contains text variables, ex: "AppName" = Application name. "AppDisplayName" = Application display name. "AppDescription" = Application description name. "AppStart" = Application start time (UTC) formatted using "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss". "AppAssemblyName" = Application assembly name (typically the exe name), "ExchangeRateService". "AppGuid" = A unique guid for this application, ex: "{CFBEDD92-341E-4EDB-96EB-C8305974EE29}". "UserName" = The environment user name, ex: "John Doe". "Is64BitProcess" = "True" if the process is running as a 64-bit process, else "False". "OSVersion" = The version of the OS. "Platform" = The platform, ex "WinNT", "Unix". "MachineName" = The computer name. "MachineNameCased" = The computer name, lower cased with the first letter upper cased. "ExeAppName", "Executable", "ExecutableDir", "ExecutableBase" = See the members with the same names. "KeyFolder" = The folder where keys are stored (). Keys are case sensitive. The dictionary is rebuilt (lazily) when the app name, display name or description changes.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.EnvInfo.TextVarsCaseInsensitive
member.summary: Contains text variables in a case insensitive dictionary where all keys are lowercased, ex: "appname" = Application name. "appdisplayname" = Application display name. "appdescription" = Application description name. "appstart" = Application start time (UTC) formatted using "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss". "appassemblyname" = Application assembly name (typically the exe name), "ExchangeRateService". "appguid" = A unique guid for this application, ex: "{CFBEDD92-341E-4EDB-96EB-C8305974EE29}". "username" = The environment user name, ex: "John Doe". "is64bitprocess" = "True" if the process is running as a 64-bit process, else "False". "osversion" = The version of the OS. "platform" = The platform, ex "WinNT", "Unix". "machinename" = The computer name. "keyfolder" = The folder where keys are stored. "machinenamecased", "exeappname", "executable", "executabledir", "executablebase" = See . The dictionary uses a case insensitive comparer, so any casing of the keys can be used for lookups.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.EnvInfo.ResolveText(System.String,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String})
member.summary: Resolve a text template that may contain env info variables, ex: "$(AppName)". $(AppName) = Application name. $(AppDisplayName) = Application display name. $(AppDescription) = Application description name. $(AppStart) = Application start time (UTC) formatted using "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss". $(AppAssemblyName) = Application assembly name (typically the exe name), "ExchangeRateService". $(AppGuid) = A unique guid for this application, ex: "{CFBEDD92-341E-4EDB-96EB-C8305974EE29}". $(UserName) = The environment user name, ex: "John Doe". $(Is64BitProcess) = "True" if the process is running as a 64-bit process, else "False". $(OSVersion) = The version of the OS. $(Platform) = The platform, ex "WinNT", "Unix". $(MachineName) = The computer name. $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored.
member.param: The template, variables start with "$(" and ends with ")". $(AppName) = Application name. $(AppDisplayName) = Application display name. $(AppDescription) = Application description name. $(AppStart) = Application start time (UTC) formatted using "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss". $(AppAssemblyName) = Application assembly name (typically the exe name), "ExchangeRateService". $(AppGuid) = A unique guid for this application, ex: "{CFBEDD92-341E-4EDB-96EB-C8305974EE29}". $(UserName) = The environment user name, ex: "John Doe". $(Is64BitProcess) = "True" if the process is running as a 64-bit process, else "False". $(OSVersion) = The version of the OS. $(Platform) = The platform, ex "WinNT", "Unix". $(MachineName) = The computer name. $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored.
If true the variable names is case in-sensitive
Optional extra variables, used for names not found in (env info variables take precedence). When case insensitive, the lookup in uses its own comparer.
member.returns: The resolved text (null or empty if is null or empty)
member.remarks: Thread safe. When no variables are given, the resolved result is cached per template (the cache is cleared when , or changes). Caches are unbounded, so don't use with an unbounded set of templates.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.EnvInfo.MakeAbsoulte(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Make an absolute path from a relative path (not using current directory, but rather the executable directory). If the path already is absolute (rooted), or is an url (contains "://"), nothing will be changed (except for directory separators).

Make relative to the current path instead of the executable path
member.returns: An absolute path, or null if is null
member.remarks: The result is not normalized, ".." segments are kept as is (no protection against path traversal).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExceptionExt.SafeText(System.Exception)

member.param: The exception, may be null

member.remarks: Stack trace source locations keeps the file name and line number (ex: "in x.cs:line 12"), the folders are removed.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExceptionExt.SafeExceptionText(System.String)
member.summary:
Remove sensitive information from an exception text (or any text that may contain one), so that it can be sent to a client.
Removed / masked (replaced with ):
File system paths (Windows drive and UNC paths, Unix paths starting with a well known root folder or "~"), only the file name (or the last folder name) is kept, ex: "C:\Users\me\app\x.cs:line 12" becomes "x.cs:line 12".
Values of secret / connection string keys (password, pwd, user id, uid, user, server, host, data source, api key, secret, token, key, sig etc) in "key=value" and json ("key": "value") form.
User info in urls (ex: "https://user:pass@host" becomes "https://***@host"), bearer and basic authorization tokens, JWT's and well known api key formats (sk-..., AKIA..., AIza..., ghp_..., xox?-...).
Private (LAN) IP addresses (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x, 169.254.x.x, fc00::/7, fe80::/10) and internal host names (*.local, *.internal, *.lan, *.corp, *.intranet, *.localdomain, *.home.arpa).
SQL details: quoted values in SQL statements, the "near '...'" fragment and "Duplicate entry '...'" value of (MySQL) syntax errors and the user / host in "Access denied for user '...'@'...'".
Kept: normal messages, file names, public IP addresses and host names, e-mail addresses, guids, numbers, assembly versions and stack trace method names.
member.param: The text, may be null
member.returns: The filtered text (the same instance if nothing was removed), null if is null
member.remarks: This is a best effort (heuristic) filter, it can't detect every kind of sensitive information (ex: secrets that aren't in a key / value form), so don't put secrets in exception messages. The regular expressions are source generated (compiled at build time) and each one is only used if the text contains a char it requires, so texts without any special chars are only scanned for tokens.

The private _message field of can't be found in the current runtime
member.remarks: Exception types that override may not return the new text. The setter is a compiled expression (created once in the static constructor), so calls are fast.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.ExceptionStackEqualityComparer
member.summary: Exceptions are deemed equal if they are of the same type and have the same stack trace (message can be different, so that time or other state information doesn't make them differ).
member.remarks: Typically used to de-duplicate logged / reported exceptions. Inner exceptions are not compared. Exceptions that were never thrown have a null , so all never thrown exceptions of the same type are equal.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.ExceptionStackEqualityComparer.Instance
member.summary: The only instance

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExceptionStackEqualityComparer.Equals(System.Exception,System.Exception)

The second exception, may be null
member.returns: True if both are null, or if both have the same type and stack trace, else false

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExceptionStackEqualityComparer.GetHashCode(System.Exception)
member.summary: Get a hash code based on the stack trace of an exception (the type isn't included).
member.param: The exception
member.returns: The hash code of the stack trace, 0 if the exception or the stack trace is null
member.remarks: String hash codes are randomized per process, so the value must not be persisted.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExternalProcess.Run(System.String,System.String,System.Action{System.String,System.Boolean},System.Action{System.Int32,System.Exception,System.TimeSpan,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String}},System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Run an external command and block until it exits (no timeout).
member.param: The command (executable) to run
Optional command arguments

Optional output callback, second parameter is false for stdout and true for stderr. Called once with the entire (trimmed) stdout after the process has closed it (if non-empty), and once per non-empty stderr line (from a background thread, exceptions are ignored). Calls are never concurrent. Never called when is true.

Optionally called when the process completed or on error, parameters are: exitCode (-1 on error), exception (null on success), duration and the captured output (the last 64 outputs, i.e the trimmed stdout and the stderr lines, in the order they were received)
The folder to use as the current, null to use the current folder of this process
Use shell execute (output is then not captured)
member.returns: The process exit code
member.exception: Any exception thrown while starting or running the process is re-thrown (after has been invoked), ex: if the executable can't be found.

Calls are never concurrent. Never called when is true.

Optionally called when the process completed or on error, parameters are: exitCode (-1 on error), exception (null on success), duration and the captured output (the last 64 outputs, i.e the trimmed stdout and the stderr lines, in the order they were received)

member.name: T:SysWeaver.FastMemCache`2
member.summary: Implements a thread safe cache that removes its items after a fixed duration (or at the time returned by an expiration function).
member.remarks: The expiration time of an item is computed when the item is added / updated, reading an item doesn't extend its life time. Expired items are never returned, they are removed (pruned) from the cache on any write (or when is called). With a fixed duration, pruning walks a queue in insertion order (the expiration times are increasing) and stops at the first item that hasn't expired. With an expiration function, the expiration times are kept in a priority queue (min-heap), so items are pruned in expiration order (a long lived item doesn't delay the pruning of other items). Items that never expire () are not tracked for pruning at all. Updates of the same key are serialized using a per key spin lock (a lock entry in a concurrent dictionary), so a value factory is only executed once for a key at the same time. The synchronous methods hold the key lock while the value factory runs (other callers for the key spin / sleep). The async methods only hold the key lock while starting an update: a running update is a pending entry, callers with waitUntilReady = true await it (without blocking a thread), callers with waitUntilReady = false get default until it's ready. Keys can't be null. The synchronous methods (GetOrUpdate etc) treat a pending entry as a cache hit and return default until the value is ready.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.FastMemCache`2.Prune
member.summary: Call to manually prune (remove) old items, no real need to call this unless memory usage is the primary concern
member.remarks: Pruning is performed automatically after every write. With a fixed duration, items are pruned in insertion order (same as expiration order), pruning stops at the first item that hasn't expired yet. With an expiration function, items are pruned in expiration order (using a priority queue). Items that are locked (being updated) at the time of the prune are pruned later.

member.summary: Perform the actual prune, moved to it's own method to make it easier for the JIT to inline the Prune method (checking for pruning)

member.summary: The core of all async updates. Only one update per key runs at a time: the key lock is only held while the cache entry is inspected and the update is started (never while awaiting), a running update is represented by a pending entry (expires never, value is default, Item3 is the task of the update). Callers with = false gets the value of the pending entry (default) while the update runs, callers with = true awaits the update (without blocking a thread). If an update fails, the caller that started it gets the exception, a failed waited update restores the previous (expired) entry, a failed background update removes the entry. Callers waiting for a failed update started by a waiting caller try again (one at a time, like when they waited for the key lock), callers waiting for a failed background update (started with = false) get the exception.

member.param: The key
The value factory supplied by the user (only used for a null check)
The state passed to
Starts the value factory: (key, existing (expired) value or default, state)
If true, wait for the update, else return default while the update runs

member.name: T:SysWeaver.FileExt
member.summary: Read and write files (whole file operations).
member.remarks: Writes are not atomic, the file is truncated first, so a failed write leaves a partial file (write to a temp file and move it if atomicity is required). Reads uses (memory mapped io on Windows, read into pooled memory on other platforms). The modes ("others can read the file while it's written", "fails while another process has the file open for writing") are only enforced by Windows. On Linux (and other Unix platforms) .NET emulates them with advisory locks (flock): takes an exclusive lock and every other mode a shared lock, so an open only fails if another .NET handle (in any process) has the file open with (or if this one uses and the file is open by another .NET handle), ex: a write succeeds while someone else reads the file with , and processes that don't use flock are never blocked.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.FileHash
member.summary: Computes and caches file hashes (automatic pruning). Folders can be overridden using the key "FileHashFolders" in the ApplicationName.Config.json file (shared with DecompressedFileHash). Default uses the Folders.AllSharedFolders locations.
member.remarks: Hashes are MD5 hashes of the file content, encoded as 26 char strings (see ), typically used as ETags / cache busters, NOT for security. The disk cache is a small text file per (file name, creation time, last write time, length) key, a file modified without changing any of these returns a stale hash. Cache files that haven't been accessed for 30 days are deleted when the process exits. Cache files are written atomically (a temp file in the same folder renamed to the cache file name), never rewritten in place, so concurrent readers / writers (threads or processes) are safe. Files are hashed using (memory mapped on Windows, read into pooled memory on other platforms).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.FileReadOnlyMemory
member.summary: Functions for getting the content of a file as memory, using memory mapped io on Windows (no copy, the OS pages the file in on demand). On other platforms (Linux, macOS etc) the data is read into pooled memory instead (see ).
member.remarks: All functions reads from the current position of the file stream to the end of the file. The returned must be disposed when no longer used (unmaps the file, or returns a pooled buffer), the memory must not be used after that. Files opened by name are opened with (on Windows others can't open the file for writing while it's open, on other platforms this is only advisory). Windows refuses to truncate a file while a view of it is mapped (ERROR_USER_MAPPED_FILE), so a mapped file can't shrink under the memory (the content may still change if the file was opened with ). On Linux / macOS nothing prevents another thread / process from truncating a mapped file, touching a mapped page past the new end raises SIGBUS, which kills the process (can't be caught), that's why files are never mapped there: the memory is a copy of the data taken when the function is called (if the file shrinks during the read, the memory is shorter). Used by for all 's, by and by the http file handler.

member.remarks: On non-Windows platforms a mapped file can be truncated by anyone that can write to it, the next access to a page past the new end of file kills the process (SIGBUS).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Folders
member.summary: Use this to get base folders for application data. Folders can be configured in the ApplicationName.Config.json config file, using the keys: - "AllFolders" for folders not specific to the running user. - "UserFolders" for folders specific to the running user (either use the "$(LocalApplicationData)" to use the OS users home folder, or the "$(UserName)"). You can optionally or additionally override any of the derived folders using the keys: - "AllSharedFolders". - "AllAppFolders". - "UserSharedFolders". - "UserAppFolders". Multiple folders can be specified, separated by the platform path separator (';' on Windows, ':' on Unix), and may contain variables. When multiple folders are available, use to distribute data among them. The key folder is configured using the "KeyFolder" key (defaults to ).
member.remarks: All folders are resolved and created (if missing) in the static constructor, which also marks them as not content indexed. Folders shared by all users are made accessible to everyone (using ), so data written by a service (ex: running as SYSTEM or root) stays modifiable by users and vice versa. On Linux "$(CommonApplicationData)" is "/var/lib" (see ), where only root can create folders: when root runs first, the "SysWeaver" root folder is created with rwx for everyone and the sticky bit (so any user can create application folders in it). If an all user folder doesn't exist and can't be created (ex: a normal user runs before root), the matching user folders are used instead ( = , = ) and a warning is written to the console.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.FrozenStringTrie
member.summary: The implementation of the frozen string trees ( and ), a tree of strings that makes it fast to check if a text starts with ANY of the contained strings. A leaf (the string, or the values of the string) is stored for every string in the tree (as an object, the derived classes have the typed public api, so that all code is compiled for the exact type). Empty strings are not supported, they can't be added and can't be searched for (throws in debug builds).
member.remarks: The tree is stored as a flat array of nodes (a compressed trie): - The children of a node are stored after each other, sorted by their first char (the first chars are stored in ). - A chain of nodes that have a single child and no string is compressed into a label (the chars after the first char), that is compared as a span. - Nodes with a lot of children have a lookup table (indexed by the char). - StartsWithAny rejects texts that are shorter than the shortest string, or starts with an ASCII char (or a pair of ASCII chars) that can't match using bit masks, before walking the tree. - Small trees (at most 32 strings of at least 4 chars, the typical use case) doesn't walk the tree in StartsWithAny, the first 4 - 8 chars (the length of the shortest string, at most 8) are looked up in a collision free hash table instead, followed by a compare of the strings that starts with them. Case in-sensitive trees use the tree if the text isn't ASCII. For case in-sensitive trees all chars (keys and labels) are upper cased (using CharExt.FastToUpper). Immutable after construction, so all searches are thread safe. The search results are equivalent to the mutable source trees ( and ).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.HttpRateLimiter
member.summary: A rate limiter for http requests, a request that is over the limit can be delayed (async) for a while instead of being rejected immediately.
member.remarks: Used by the http server to limit requests per server, per api and per session (a rejected request typically returns http status 429). Waiting requests poll the limit (they are not queued in order), so they are not served in a fair (FIFO) order.

member.summary: Number of requests that are currently delayed (waiting for a free slot)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.HttpRateLimiter.IsOverTheLimit
member.summary: Check if a request is over the limit, if it is, the request may be delayed (async) until a slot is free.
member.returns: False if the request is allowed (possibly after a delay), true if the limit is exceeded and the request should be rejected (return 429). The returned value task is completed synchronously (no allocation) if the request is within the limit
member.remarks: A request is rejected immediately if requests are already delayed, or if the remaining allowed delay () isn't enough to reach a free slot

member.summary: An inspector visits the data of an object, the same interface is used for reading (the inspector assigns values), writing (the inspector reads values) and other operations (copy, compare etc). objects describe themselves by calling the methods of an inspector for each member.
member.remarks: The Field methods take a reference that is read and/or assigned, the Prop methods take the current value and an optional setter that is called when the inspector assigns a new value (a null setter means that the value is only written, not read back). Implementations are typically not thread safe.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.IO.LengthLimitedStream
member.summary: A read only view of a part of another stream, starting at the current position of the stream and limited to a maximum length. Typically used to let a decoder read a chunk of a file without being able to read past it (ex: PNG IDAT chunks).
member.remarks: The underlying stream must be seekable (the position is used to compute the remaining length) and is NOT disposed by this stream. Reads and seeks moves the position of the underlying stream, so the underlying stream must not be used at the same time.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.LimitedObjectPool`1
member.summary: A concurrent object pool with a limited number of cached objects. There is a small chance that the number of objects exceeds the maximum. The object must implement IDisposable and call the supplied Action there. Do not perform any actual disposing of required internal resources, resetting the object for re-use is fine. If disposing of required internal resources is required, supply a disposer that will be called when an instance in no longer needed.

member.remarks: The pool is lock free, cached objects are re-used in LIFO order (the most recently returned object is returned first). Objects must only be returned (disposed) once per .

member.name: T:SysWeaver.LowAllocConcurrentDictionary`2
member.summary:
A concurrent dictionary designed for (very) large data sets, with as few and as small memory allocations as possible. No memory is allocated per item, each segment stores the items inline in a few arrays (allocated when growing), so the GC only sees a few hundred objects regardless of the number of items.
The keys are split into segments, each segment is an open addressing hash table protected by a spin lock. All modifications are done while holding the segment lock. Reads are lock free, they are validated using a per segment version (seqlock) and retried if a write happened during the read. Writes also search for the key lock free before taking the lock (so that the cache misses don't happen while holding it), the result is used if the segment version is the same when the lock is taken.
member.remarks: Thread safe, all operations can be called concurrently. Null keys are not allowed (). Ordinal string keys (the default string comparer or ) use a fast, randomly seeded hash, a segment that sees many collisions switches to the randomized ordinal hash (hash flooding protection). The segment locks are spin locks, so keep comparers and hash functions cheap. , , and return snapshots (new collections), enumeration is weakly consistent (see ). Removed entries leave tombstones that are cleaned up when a segment is rebuilt (memory is not returned until then).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.MovingAverage
member.summary: Computes the moving average (and rates) of some value within a sliding time window. - Thread safe. - Accurate: the rates are computed over the full window (or the time since this instance was created if that is less than the window), so the result is correct even if there are only one or two samples in the window, or if the samples stopped coming in a while ago. - Bounded memory: samples that are closer in time than 1/1024 of the window are merged (so the window edge has a precision of 1/1024 of the window). - Allocation free (except when the internal buffer has to grow, at most log2(2048 / InitSize) times).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.ObjectMerger
member.summary: Contains a static cache that can merge identical immutable objects
member.remarks: Two objects are considered identical if they are of the exact same type and all their public readable instance properties (excluding indexers) are equal. Property values that are enumerable (strings, arrays, lists etc) are compared element wise (recursively), other property values are compared using their Equals method. If the object itself is enumerable, it's elements are also part of the identity. Public fields, non-public properties and static properties are not part of the identity. The cache is a least recently used cache (a ): an object that isn't used for (5 minutes) is removed, so the memory used is bounded by the objects used recently (expr-cov-15: objects were kept forever). An identical object passed after that becomes the new shared instance.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.ObjectMerger.TypeProperties
member.summary: The properties of a type that makes up the identity of an instance (cached per type, reflection is slow)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ObjectMerger.GetShared``1(``0)
member.summary: Try to merge this immutable object
member.typeparam: Type of the object, only use immutable types!
member.param: The object that should be merged with any other objects representing the same thing
member.returns: The input object or an object representing the same thing (the cached instance)
member.exception: is null
A property getter of threw an exception
member.remarks: The cache is global and thread safe, the first instance (with a given identity) that is passed to this method is returned for all subsequent calls with an identical object, as long as it's used: an instance that isn't used for is removed (and the next identical object passed becomes the shared instance). See for a description of what makes two objects identical. Mutating an object after it have been merged is undefined behavior.

member.remarks: Calls where the type argument is a value type are never counted.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.ObjectMerger.Timeout
member.summary: The time an object is kept in the cache after it was last used (the default is 5 minutes). An object is removed when it hasn't been used for this time, an object used within the last half of it is always kept. Setting it replaces the cache (all cached objects are dropped); zero or negative: nothing is cached (no objects are merged), : objects are kept forever.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.StripExtension(System.String)
member.summary: Remove the extension from a path. Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\Data.dll" to "C:\Windows\Temp\Data" Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt" to "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt"
member.param: A path with an extension. Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\Data.dll" to "C:\Windows\Temp\Data" Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt" to "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt"
member.returns: The path without an extension or the original path (same instance) if non exist. Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\Data.dll" to "C:\Windows\Temp\Data" Example: "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt" to "C:\Windows\Temp\NoExt"
member.remarks: Only the last '.' is removed (along with everything after it), so "a.tar.gz" becomes "a.tar". A '.' in a directory name (followed by a '/' or '\') is not considered to be an extension, both '/' and '\' are treated as separators on all platforms. A file name starting with a '.' (ex: ".gitignore") is treated as an extension, so the file name part becomes empty.
member.exception: is null (debug builds only; release builds throw a ).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.IsValidFilename(System.String)
member.summary: Check if a filename without a path is valid, ex: "Filename.txt".
member.param: The filename to test
member.returns: True if valid (no invalid file name or path chars, and no volume, path or directory separators), only way to make sure is to actuallty try to use it though. An empty string is considered valid.
member.remarks: The rules of the OS that the process runs on are used (, and the separators of ): on Windows the control chars (0-31), '"', '<', '>', '|', '*', '?', ':', ';', '\' and '/' are invalid, on Linux (and other Unix platforms) only '\0', '/' and ':' (the path separator) are invalid, so ex: "a\b", "a*b" or "a|b" are valid file names there.
member.exception: is null.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.IsValidFolderPath(System.String)
member.summary: Check if a folder with a path is valid, ex: "C:\Windows\System32".
member.param: The path to the directory to test
member.returns: True if valid, only way to make sure is to actuallty try to use it though. Invalid paths contains invalid path chars, a path separator (';' on Windows), more than one ':' or two consecutive directory separators (except at the start, to allow UNC paths). An empty string is considered valid.
member.remarks: The rules of the OS that the process runs on are used: on Windows the invalid chars are '|', '\0', the control chars and ';', and both '\' and '/' are directory separators. On Linux (and other Unix platforms) the invalid chars are '\0' and ':' (the path separator, so a Windows path like "C:\Windows" is invalid) and only '/' is a directory separator ('\' is a valid file name char).
member.exception: is null.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.IsValidFilePath(System.String)
member.summary: Check if a file with a path is valid, ex: "C:\Windows\System32\Filename.txt".
member.param: The path to the file to test
member.returns: True if valid, only way to make sure is to actuallty try to use it though. The part after the last volume or directory separator must be a valid file name (see ) and the part before it must be a valid folder path (see ). The rules (separators and invalid chars) of the OS that the process runs on are used, on Linux a Windows path like "C:\Filename.txt" is invalid (':') and "a\b.txt" is a valid file name.
member.exception: is null.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.SafeFilename(System.String)

member.returns: A string of the same length as the input where every char that is invalid in a file name (see ) is replaced with a '_'. If no chars needs to be replaced (or if the input is null or empty) the input instance is returned. The rules of the OS that the process runs on are used: on Linux only '\0', '/' and ':' are replaced (ex: "a\b*c" is kept as is), so the result may not be a valid file name on Windows.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathExt.AllowAllAccess(System.String)
member.summary: Allow all users to read / write a folder (on Windows: adds a full control rule for "Everyone"). On other platforms of is used (Linux: "a+rwX" on the folder and all content plus a POSIX default ACL, see the SysWeaver.Common.Linux LinuxPlatformTools).
member.remarks: The rule is container and object inherited (), so it applies to the folder and is inherited by all nested files and sub folders (at any depth). This makes files and folders created by a service (ex: running as SYSTEM) modifiable by users (without an UAC prompt) and vice versa. Applying the rule to an existing folder also propagates it to the existing files and sub folders that inherit permissions (Windows does this when the security descriptor is written). A rule added by older versions (using , only inherited by direct children) is replaced. Granting everyone full control makes the folder writable by any local user, only use it for data that isn't security sensitive. On Linux the mode bits (rwx for everyone and setgid on folders, rw on files) are applied to the folder and all of it's content, but only the owner (or root) can change them, and the default ACL (for entries created later) requires the "setfacl" tool (package "acl"): if it's missing, the mode bits are still applied but false is returned. If the platform assembly (SysWeaver.Common.Linux) isn't deployed, nothing is done and true is returned.
member.param: The folder
member.returns: True if successful (or if the folder doesn't exist or the platform has no implementation), false on error (never throws)

member.name: T:SysWeaver.PathTemplate
member.summary: Resolve a "path" template to a full path. Variables in the template starts with "$(" and ends with ")". Variables can be any value of the Environment.SpecialFolder enum, or any of the ones in the supplied dictionary. Ex: "$(LocalApplicationData)\MyAppsData\StateBlockUntil.json" Some common folder variables: $(CommonApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by all users. $(LocalApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by the current, non-roaming user. $(ApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data for the current roaming user (typically settings that should be shared between systems). $(MyPictures) = The My Pictures folder. Env info variables: $(Executable) = Full path to the executable, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService.exe" $(ExeAppName) = Name of the executable, ex: "MyService" (this can be different from AppName) $(ExecutableDir) = ExecutableDir, ex: "C:\MyServices" $(ExecutableBase) = Full path to the executable, excluding it's extensions, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService" $(AppName) = Application name (defaults to exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "MyService". $(AppGuid) = A guid derived from the application assembly name (stable between runs) $(AppDisplayName) = Friendly application name (defaults to de-camel cased exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "My service". $(MachineName) = Machine name, ex: "DESKTOP-324VHA". $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored. ex: "C:\Keys". See for all env info variables.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.PathTemplate.CommonApplicationData
member.summary: The folder for application data shared by all users, this is what "$(CommonApplicationData)" resolves to. Windows (and other platforms): , ex: "C:\ProgramData". Linux: "/var/lib" (.NET returns "/usr/share", which is meant for read only data).
member.remarks: On Linux only root can create folders in "/var/lib", see for how the SysWeaver folder is set up.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PathTemplate.Resolve(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String},System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Resolve a "path" template to a full path. Variables in the template starts with "$(" and ends with ")". Variables can be any value of the Environment.SpecialFolder enum, or any of the ones in the supplied dictionary. Formatting as described in the TextTemplate type can be used ("$(*Var)" is useful for paths). Ex: "$(LocalApplicationData)\MyAppsData\StateBlockUntil.json" Some common folders: $(CommonApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by all users. $(LocalApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data that is used by the current, non-roaming user. $(ApplicationData) = The directory that serves as a common repository for application-specific data for the current roaming user (typically settings that should be shared between systems). $(MyPictures) = The My Pictures folder.
member.param: The template, variables start with "$(" and ends with ")".
Optional extra variables. If case insensitive is specified, the keys in this dictionary must be lower-cased (names are lower cased before the lookup)
If true the variable names is case in-sensitive

If true, variables from EnvInfo.TextVars are available, examples: $(Executable) = Full path to the executable, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService.exe" $(ExeAppName) = Name of the executable, ex: "MyService" (this can be different from AppName) $(ExecutableDir) = ExecutableDir, ex: "C:\MyServices" $(ExecutableBase) = Full path to the executable, excluding it's extensions, ex: "C:\MyServices\MyService" $(AppName) = Application name (defaults to exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "MyService". $(AppGuid) = A guid derived from the application assembly name (stable between runs) $(AppDisplayName) = Friendly application name (defaults to de-camel cased exe app name, can be changed in config), ex: "My service". $(MachineName) = Machine name, ex: "DESKTOP-324VHA". $(KeyFolder) = The folder where keys are stored. ex: "C:\Keys".
member.returns: The resolved path (null or empty if is null or empty). The result is not made absolute (see ).
member.remarks: Lookup order: special folders ( names), then , then env info variables. Only defined special folder names are resolved as folders (numeric values are not). How unknown variables are handled is defined by . Parsed templates are cached per template string (thread safe, unbounded), the variables are evaluated on every call.

A loop that was stopped () or that ended by itself (the function returned false, or threw with continueOnException false) can be started again (), every start uses a new cancellation token (). member.name: T:SysWeaver.PrefixFinder
member.summary: Provides a fast way to determine what a string starts with (from a given fixed set), the string to test MUST start with one in the set.
member.remarks: The prefixes are expected to be URL's: everything up to and including the host is stripped from every prefix ("https://host/api/" becomes "/api/"), so the texts to test should be the path part of an URL (a prefix without "://" is used as is). Not used by the framework.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PrefixFinder.StripPrefix(System.String)
member.summary: Get the path part of an URL ("https://host/a/b" => "/a/b", "https://host" => "")
member.returns: The path (starting with a '/'), an empty string if there is no path, or the string as is if it doesn't contain "://"

member.name: M:SysWeaver.PrefixFinder.Create(System.String[],System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a prefix finder. If all (stripped) prefixes differs at some char position (shorter than the shortest prefix), the result is a lookup of that single char (an array lookup if the chars are within a range of 256), else the prefixes are tested in order of decreasing length (the longest matching prefix is returned).
member.param: The URL's whose path part should be matched against, ex: ["https://host/api/", "https://host/files/"] (matches "/api/" and "/files/"). A prefix without "://" is used as is (ex: "/api/"). Duplicate paths are merged
True if the comparison should be case sensitive, else false (ASCII and invariant culture case folding)
member.returns: A function that given a string (an URL path), returns the (stripped) prefix that it starts with. The given string must start with one of the pre-defined prefixes or the behaviour is undefined (it may return a wrong prefix, String.Empty or throw an IndexOutOfRangeException). If no prefixes are given the function always returns String.Empty, if one is given that prefix is always returned. When several prefixes match, the longest one is returned

member.name: T:SysWeaver.QuickHash
member.summary: Tools for computing a 32-bit hash fast. This is NOT a secure hash, do not use for security! The hash is endian specific, meaning that a hash computed over some data on a little endian machine differs from the hash computed on a big endian machine (so do not use for data transport etc).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.QuickHash.Hash(System.String,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Compute a 32-bit hash for a string. This is NOT a secure hash, do not use for security! The hash is endian specific, meaning that a hash computed over some text on a little endian machine differs from the hash computed on a big endian machine (so do not use for data transport etc).
member.param: The text to compute a hash over
An optional seed (defaults to 0xc58f1a7b)
member.returns: A 32-bit hash of the text, 0 if the text is null or empty
member.remarks: The hash is computed over the UTF-16 representation of the text, i.e. it's the same as hashing the bytes of the chars

member.name: M:SysWeaver.QuickHash.Hash(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte},System.UInt32)
member.summary: Compute a 32-bit hash over some data. This is NOT a secure hash, do not use for security! The hash is endian specific, meaning that a hash computed over some data on a little endian machine differs from the hash computed on a big endian machine (so do not use for data transport etc).
member.param: The data to compute a hash over
An optional seed (defaults to 0xc58f1a7b)
member.returns: A 32-bit hash of the data, 0 if the data is empty
member.remarks: This is MurmurHash2 (on little endian machines), except that empty data always hash to 0 (regardless of the seed)

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Scheduler
member.summary: Schedules a task to be performed at a specified time, precision is fairly low so the task can be executed a few seconds later than scheduled. Use this for low frequency tasks that should run on a schedule, once a day, once per hour and so on. For high frequency tasks use the PeriodicTask instead.
member.remarks: A single process wide checks the schedule every ms while there are scheduled entries (it's stopped when the schedule is empty). An entry never runs concurrently with itself. Exceptions thrown by tasks are recorded on the entry and in . Disposing an entry waits for a running execution to complete, except when called from within the entry's own task (then it returns immediately and the entry is not re-scheduled).

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Scheduler.CheckFrequencyMs
member.summary: Roughly the number of milli seconds between each check

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Scheduler.Add(System.DateTime,System.Action,System.String,System.Func{System.DateTime,System.DateTime},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Schedule a task to be performed at a specified time, precision is fairly low so the task can be executed a few seconds later than scheduled. Use this for low frequency tasks that should run on a schedule, once a day, once per hour and so on. For high frequency tasks use the PeriodicTask instead.
member.param: The time to execute the task at (a non UTC time, including , is treated as local time and converted to UTC), precision is fairly low so the task can be executed a few seconds later than scheduled. A time in the past executes the task at the next check.
The task to execute (on the thread pool)
An optional name (for debugging)

An optional function that is executed after the task completed to re-schedule the task, given the previous scheduled execution time (UTC), returns the next execution time (that must be later). It's called repeatedly until a time in the future is returned (so missed executions are skipped). If it returns a time that isn't later than it's input, the entry is not re-scheduled and the error is recorded in .
If true the task runs in it's own async chain (independent of other tasks), else all non async tasks that are due at the same check are executed one after another in a shared async chain
member.returns: The scheduled , dispose it to prevent execution of the task in the future (disposing blocks until a currently running execution has completed, unless called from within the task itself)

member.name: T:SysWeaver.SemiFrozenDictionary`2
member.summary: A dictionary for data where the number of reads far exceeds the number of modifications. This is thread safe in the same sense as a . Reads are done on a frozen copy of the underlying dictionary (see ). Modifications of the underlying dictionary are done while holding a lock, and the frozen copy is invalidated. After a modification, reads are done on the underlying (concurrent) dictionary until it has been read enough times without modifications to make freezing it worth the cost (freezing allocates a copy, so freezing after every modification of a growing cache would be O(n^2)).
member.remarks: Reads are lock free, modifications are serialized (a single lock per dictionary). A read that races with a modification may see the state before the modification. , and enumeration operate on a snapshot (they force a freeze if needed). Null keys are not allowed (, frozen or not).

member.summary: The frozen copy, null after a modification (until it has been read enough times to freeze it again)

member.summary: The number of reads of the underlaying dictionary since the last modification (not exact, it's incremented without synchronization)

member.name: F:SysWeaver.SemiFrozenDictionary`2.FreezeAfter
member.summary: Freeze when this number of reads have been done since the last modification. A frozen copy is faster to read, but it costs about as much to create as 16 extra reads per item (of the underlaying dictionary), so freezing when the extra cost of the reads equals the cost of freezing is never more than twice as expensive as the best choice.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.SingleTaskRunner
member.summary: A class than let's you spawn an async task. Will wait for any previous task to complete before starting the new one. If a previous task throws an exception, the Start or Wait method will throw that exception.
member.remarks: Tasks are run one at a time, in the order that the Start calls acquire the internal lock. An exception thrown by a task is only reported once (by the next Start or Wait call), the original stack trace is preserved. The internal lock is held while a task runs, so calling Start or Wait from within a running task will wait forever.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.StringPrefixLookupBase
member.summary: The implementation of the string prefix lookups ( and ), finds the longest string (from a set of strings) that a text starts with, using ordinal (case sensitive) compares. A leaf (the string, or an entry with the value) is stored for every string (as an object, the derived classes have the typed public api, so that all code is compiled for the exact type). Optimized for a few (up to ~32) short strings (4 - 16 chars), where most searches doesn't match, like the web page sub paths of special modules. Empty strings are not supported, they can't be added (throws an ) and can't be searched for (throws in debug builds).
member.remarks: If all strings have at least 4 chars (and there are at most 254 strings): - Texts that are shorter than the shortest string, or starts with an ASCII char that no string starts with, are rejected. - The key is the first K chars of the text (K is the length of the shortest string, at most 8), loaded as two integers (the first 4 chars and the last 4 chars of the key, overlapping if K is less than 8), and hashed to a slot. The slot have a chain of entries (the strings that hash to the slot, longest first). - An entry is a match if the key and the last 8 chars of the string (as a vector, or the last 4 chars as an integer for strings shorter than 8 chars) are equal to the text (and the chars in between, for long strings). - The hash multipliers are selected to minimize the collisions (typically there are none), so a miss is (typically) a hash and a compare. Else (or if 128 bit vectors aren't hardware accelerated) a case sensitive is used. Immutable after construction, so it's safe to use from multiple threads.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.StringTools
member.summary: General string helpers: quoting and formatting, casing of words, white space clean up, fuzzy matching (Levenstein), char classification and filtering, hex conversions, splitting, masking ("secure") of secrets, line splitting and markdown escaping.
member.remarks: Most methods avoid temporary allocations (stack or pooled buffers) and return the input instance if nothing changes. Unless stated otherwise, the string arguments may not be null. All methods are thread safe.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.StringTree
member.summary: A string tree (a mutable trie with one dictionary per node) stores a bunch of strings in a way that makes it fast to check if a test string starts with ANY of the contained strings. Empty strings are not supported, they can't be added (throws an ) and can't be searched for (throws in debug builds).
member.remarks: The root node is the tree, and the leaf of the root is used as the case in-sensitive marker. Case in-sensitive trees upper case all chars (invariant culture, see ), the found strings are the added strings (original casing). Not thread safe for writes (concurrent reads without writes are safe). In debug builds every node have a finalizer (used to maintain the AllocatedNodes diagnostics counter, that only exists in debug builds). Use (built from a ) for a faster immutable version.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.StringValidate.IpV6(System.String)
member.summary: Validate that the input is valid for an IPv6 address, with an optional "/prefix length" (1 - 128). The address must have eight groups of 1 - 4 hex digits separated by ':', where one run of zero groups may be compressed to "::" (ex: "fe80::1", "::", "1:2:3:4:5:6:7::"). The last group(s) may be an embedded IPv4 address (ex: "::ffff:192.168.0.1"), counting as two groups. Zone ids ("%eth0") and brackets ("[::1]") are not accepted.
member.param: The string to test
member.exception: The address is null or invalid

If true, the last group may be an IPv4 address

member.exception: A group is invalid

member.name: M:SysWeaver.StringValidate.DomainName(System.String)
member.summary: Validate that the input is valid for a Domain name (IPv4, IPv6 address, DNS or Computer name). The type is detected from the format: a ':' is an IPv6 address (possibly with an embedded IPv4 address), no '.' is a computer name, a numeric last part (after the last '.') is an IPv4 address, else it's a DNS name. The detected type is then validated.
member.param: The string to test
member.returns: The type of domain
member.exception: The name is null, empty or invalid (for the detected type)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.TaskExt.WhenAll``1(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask{``0}})
member.summary: Creates a task that will complete when all of the supplied tasks have completed.
member.typeparam: The result type of the tasks
member.param: The tasks to wait on for completion.
member.returns: A task that represents the completion of all of the supplied tasks, the result contains the results of the tasks in the same order as the supplied tasks.

remarks.para: If any of the supplied tasks completes in a faulted state, the returned task will also complete in a Faulted state, where its exceptions will contain the aggregation of the set of unwrapped exceptions from each of the supplied tasks.
If none of the supplied tasks faulted but at least one of them was canceled, the returned task will end in the Canceled state.
If none of the tasks faulted and none of the tasks were canceled, the resulting task will end in the RanToCompletion state.
If the supplied list contains no tasks, or all tasks are already completed successfully, the returned task is completed synchronously (no task is allocated).
Every value task is awaited exactly once, the list is read again (by index) after the returned task was created, so it must not be changed until the returned task completes.

member.exception: The argument was null.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.TernaryTree`1
member.summary: A ternary search tree, a map from (non empty) string keys to values that supports prefix, wildcard and near (Hamming distance) searches.
member.remarks: Not thread safe for writes (reads concurrent with writes are also unsafe). A null value is treated as "no value", so prefix nodes and keys with a null value are indistinguishable. For non nullable value types every node counts as having a value, so prefix and near searches also return the default value for intermediate nodes. All operations are recursive (the stack depth is proportional to the key length plus the tree depth). Not used by the framework.

member.summary: Creates a text template, that can be used to replace variable (or any string) in a text quickly. Variables can either be known up front by supplying a set or dictionary, or be defined by a start and end token. Variable values can be transformed by prepending the variable name with one of the following: _ = Make lower case, ex: "hello world!". ^ = Make upper case, ex: "HELLO WORLD!". ~ = Remove camel case, ex: "MyCoolType" => "My cool type". @ = Make html attribute safe (HttpUtility.HtmlAttributeEncode), ex: "Hello world!". # = Make html value safe (HttpUtility.HtmlEncode), ex: "Hello world!". % = Make URL safe (HttpUtility.UrlEncode), ex: "Hello+world!". $ = Make javascript string safe (HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode), ex: "Hello world!". £ = Make javascript string safe with quotes (HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode), ex: var x = $(£Var); => var x = "Hello world!". ¤ = Make javascript string safe with quotes of html content (HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode(HttpUtility.HtmlEncode()), ex: var x = $(¤Var); => var x = "12 < 42". * = Make file/path safe (PathExt.SafeFilename), ex: "C:\Apa" => "C__Apa". Only one of _ , ^ and ~ may be used. Only one of @, #, %, $, £, ¤ and * may be used. _ , ^ and ~ can be combined with one of @, #, %, $, £, ¤ and *, ex: _#, ^$
member.remarks: The template text is parsed once (in the constructor), then builds the result with a single string allocation. Instances are immutable and is thread safe (as long as the value provider is). The value provider is called more than once per variable (once to compute the length and once per occurrence), so it must return the same value for the same name during a call. How unresolved variables (the provider returns null) are rendered depends on the constructor, see each constructor. Typically used for path templates (), environment variables () and HTML / text templates in the HTTP server.
