member.name: T:SysWeaver.TypeFinder
member.summary: Finds types by name, in the assemblies that are loaded, in the assemblies (dll files) in the executable folder and in the trusted platform assemblies of the runtime (the framework and app assemblies the host lists in "TRUSTED_PLATFORM_ASSEMBLIES", the assemblies that default probing would load). No other location is ever searched. Assemblies loaded into a collectible (ex: scripts) are never searched, so that they can be unloaded.
member.remarks:
is for trusted names (manifests, configuration, code), is for names that comes from (untrusted) serialized data ("$type"), it resolves the same way but only returns types that are allowed by the .
Performance:
Successfully resolved names are cached (at most names per cache, since the same type can be named in many ways).
Failed lookups are cached in separate caches (at most names per cache), that are cleared whenever an assembly is loaded (or is called), since a name may resolve after that.
The loaded assemblies are indexed once (by simple name), assemblies loaded later are added using the event, so they are never scanned again.
The executable folder is listed once (the first time an assembly that isn't loaded is requested), see .
The trusted platform assemblies list is parsed once (the first time an assembly that isn't loaded, nor in the executable folder, is requested).
A failed lookup that isn't cached costs a few hash lookups (and a per loaded assembly for names without an assembly), it never touches the disc.
Assemblies are loaded into the default load context (), so the types are identical to types loaded by references. Thread safe.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.TypeFinder.Get(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Get the type for a given (trusted) type name.
member.param: The name of the type to find, a full type name, ex: "System.String", an assembly qualified name, ex: "MyNamespace.MyType, MyAssembly", generic types are supported, ex: "System.Collections.Generic.List`1[[MyNamespace.MyType, MyAssembly]]"
If true, always return null instead of throwing
member.returns: The type or null if it can't be found (or if is null or empty)
member.remarks: Names without an assembly are searched for in all loaded (non collectible) assemblies (System.Private.CoreLib first). An assembly that isn't loaded is loaded from the executable folder ("AssemblyName.dll"), or if it's not there, from the trusted platform assemblies (ex: framework assemblies that aren't loaded yet). The lookup is case sensitive. Failed lookups are cached (until an assembly is loaded), when is false the name is always resolved again (so that the error can be thrown). Don't use this for names from untrusted input, use .
member.exception: If is false, and the assembly isn't loaded, doesn't exist in the executable folder and isn't a trusted platform assembly
If is false, any exception thrown while loading the assembly (ex: FileLoadException, BadImageFormatException) or parsing the name

member.name: M:SysWeaver.TypeFinder.GetForData(System.String,System.Type)
member.summary: Get the type for a type name that comes from (untrusted) serialized data, such as a "$type" member.
member.param: The name of the type (see for the syntax)
The type that the value must be assignable to (the declared type), null for any type
member.returns: The type, or null if no type with that name exists (or if is null or empty)
member.remarks: Resolves exactly like (loaded assemblies, the executable folder and the trusted platform assemblies), with a case insensitive fallback, and if the type isn't found in the named assembly (or the assembly doesn't exist), the type name (without the assembly) is searched for in all loaded assemblies (types that moved to another assembly). The and checks always applies to the resolved type (including the fallbacks). Never throws for unknown types or assemblies, assembly load errors are treated as not found. Failed lookups are cached (until an assembly is loaded). Names longer than chars or with generic arguments nested deeper than levels are not resolved (returns null), since every distinct generic instantiation creates a new runtime type that is never released.

member.summary: An open addressing (linear probing) hash table for more than 8 keys of a 4 or 8 byte integer (or enum) type, using the default comparer (see ). The size is a power of 2 (at most 75% used), a key is hashed using a multiply and shift (Fibonacci hashing), a slot without a key contains a value that isn't a key. member.name: M:SysWeaver.WebPath.IsRoot(System.String)
member.summary: Check if a web path is rooted, i.e it contains a scheme and a server (contains "://"), example: "https://example.com/a/b.html".

member.returns: True if the web path contains "://", else false
member.exception: If is null

member.name: M:SysWeaver.WebPath.SplitServerLocal(System.String@,System.String@,System.String)
member.summary: Split a web path into the server part (scheme, server, port and the first '/') and the local part (the rest). Example: "https://example.com/a/b.html" => "https://example.com/" and "a/b.html".
member.param: The server part (including the trailing '/' if present), an empty string if the web path isn't rooted
The local part (without the leading '/' that ends the server part), the whole web path if it isn't rooted
The web path to split
member.returns: True if the web path is rooted (contains "://"), else false
member.exception: If is null
member.remarks: server + local is always equal to the web path

member.name: M:SysWeaver.WebPath.Collapse(System.String)
member.summary: Remove all "." segments and resolve all ".." segments in the local part of a web path. Examples: "a/./b/../c.html" => "a/c.html", "https://example.com/a/../b/" => "https://example.com/b/".
member.param: The web path to collapse
member.returns: The collapsed web path (the same instance if nothing could be collapsed)
member.exception: If is null
member.remarks: The server part (if any) is never changed. A ".." that can't be resolved is kept in a relative path ("a/../../b" => "../b"), and removed in an absolute local path ("/../b" => "/b"). A trailing "." or ".." is a directory, so the result ends with a '/' ("a/b/.." => "a/", "a/." => "a/", ".." => "../"). Empty segments are kept ("a//b" => "a//b"). No allocations are made if nothing can be collapsed, else only the resulting string is allocated.

member.summary: Collapse the segments of a local path into a buffer

member.returns: The number of chars written to the buffer
